stories.headline: Enzo Maresca plays down Erling Haaland injury fears after Man City star limps off
stories.summary: Enzo Maresca has played down fears over Erling Haaland's fitness after the striker limped off at the end of Manchester City's 3-2 win over Ipswich.
stories.body:
Enzo Maresca has played down fears over Erling Haaland's fitness after the striker limped off at the end of Manchester City's 3-2 win over Ipswich on Saturday.

Haaland, who scored twice, looked in pain after a heavy challenge with Jack Clarke in stoppage time.

The Norwegian was already heading off the pitch before the full-time whistle was blown and went straight down the tunnel at the end of the game.

"We will see," Maresca said afterward. "Erling said he was OK. I don't have any news at the moment."

Haaland was one of a number of injury worries for City during the game.

Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes, Nico O'Reilly and Antoine Semenyo all picked up problems, with Maresca identifying Semenyo's as the most serious issue.

"Unfortunately in 10 minutes we had four or five players [injured] -- Matheus, Kova, Erling, Antoine and Nico also -- but they are inside now and we will see," the City boss said.

"I asked all of them. Mateo and Kova said they were OK. Erling also said he was OK and Nico, it's still his back if you remember [the injury] against Coventry. It's still the same problem. The only one we need to wait on is Antoine."

stories.headline: Dream's Allisha Gray expected to play in Game 1 of WNBA Finals
stories.summary: Dream coach Karl Smesko was optimistic that forward Allisha Gray would return from a finger injury to play in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals vs. the Valkyries.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Atlanta Dream coach Karl Smesko was optimistic that forward Allisha Gray would return from a finger injury to play in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday against the Golden State Valkyries, and she was declared available to play ahead of tipoff.

Smesko said he didn't anticipate any restrictions for his star player as the top two defensive teams in the league face off.

"She's going to go through the workout today. Everything's trending in the right direction," Smesko said before the opener in the best-of-seven series at sold-out Chase Center. "It's a hand injury, so if she can go, I don't expect there to be anything [limiting] other than if she has trouble with it during the game."

Gray participated in light practice Friday after missing the last two games of the Dream's sweep of the New York Liberty in the best-of-five semifinal series with an injured left ring finger on her shooting hand.

Gray, 31, led the team in scoring in the regular season at 19 points per game.

The Valkyries have sold out every game at Chase Center during their two years of existence, and the raucous, violet-crazed "Ballhalla" home crowd has been deafening this postseason. It makes for a frenzied scene as opposing teams visit.

Atlanta hadn't done any specific preparations for the noise.

"We do understand how loud it is here and how supportive their fans are and what a great atmosphere and environment they've provided the W," Smesko said. "So we understand what we're in for."

So do the Valkyries.

"We understand that Ballhalla's going to be rocking," said Golden State coach Natalie Nakase, who this week challenged the fans to do their own game-planning for Game 1.

stories.headline: Bears CB Kyler Gordon set for 2026 debut after PUP activation
stories.summary: Bears nickel corner Kyler Gordon has been activated off the PUP list and could make his season debut against the Falcons.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- Chicago Bears nickel corner Kyler Gordon has been activated off the physically unable to perform list and onto the 53-man roster, the team announced Saturday.

Gordon spent the offseason rehabbing a calf injury that landed him on the PUP list at the start of training camp. He was moved to reserve/PUP on Aug. 30 and had to sit out the Bears' first four games.

He returned to practice Sept. 30 and has been a full participant in every session over the past three weeks.

"He's done a great job taking everything that we've assigned him so far," coach Ben Johnson said Friday. "I feel good about him -- whether that's this week or next week -- I do feel good about him being able to contribute to this team and help us out, and there's a number of ways he can do that. But I'm encouraged with what I've seen so far."

In a corresponding move, the Bears placed defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo on injured reserve. Odeyingbo had already been ruled out for Week 6 with a quad injury sustained against the Green Bay Packers last week. Coach Ben Johnson said this week that Odeyingbo was expected to miss "some time" but that the Bears did not believe his injury was serious enough to warrant IR.

The Bears also released Xavier Woods, who started the last two games at safety, and signed defensive back Nick McCloud from the practice squad to the active roster.

Gordon was drafted 39th overall in 2022, the first-ever pick by Bears general manager Ryan Poles. Since then, the cornerback has totaled five interceptions, 17 passes defensed, 2.5 sacks, 10 tackles for loss and two forced fumbles.

Injuries were present during his first three seasons (2022-24) but did not stop the Bears from making him the NFL's highest-paid primary slot corner in April 2025 when he signed a three-year, $40 million extension with $31.25 million guaranteed.

Since signing his new deal, Gordon has struggled to stay on the field. He was limited to five games, including the playoffs, in 2025 due to multiple soft tissue injuries and spent two separate stints on injured reserve.

Last season, Gordon allowed 16 receptions on 24 targets for 243 yards and three touchdowns, according to Next Gen Stats. He allowed a passer rating of 139.4 in coverage, which was the third highest in the NFL among cornerbacks (minimum 20 targets), with only Trevon Diggs (154.6) and McCloud (142.2) allowing a higher passer rating.

After being sidelined for the Bears' offseason program and training camp, Gordon spent several weeks away from the team in September rehabbing on his own. He returned to Halas Hall ahead of Week 4 and made an impression on his coaches for how quickly he got up to speed on the practice field and in meetings.

"The one thing about Kyler, he's a sharp kid, or young man, I should say," Bears nickels coach Cannon Matthews said. "So that part I'm not worried about. Even just him being back in meetings, the questions that he asks has always been great that way. So honestly, there's still area for growth in that department, but I don't have any issue with him getting caught up to speed with the mental aspect."

The Bears could use some reinforcements in the secondary after Packers quarterback Jordan Love had six completions of 25-plus yards in Chicago's 31-7 loss.

Gordon has not played since the Bears-Rams divisional playoff matchup in January, so it is unrealistic to think he could play a full workload of 50 to 70 snaps, according to defensive coordinator Dennis Allen.

"I've said this before, I think that Kyler can help us win games," Allen said. "You know, when that time comes where he's able to be out there on the field and participate and help us win games, I'm looking forward to that time."

stories.headline: Rain postpones ALCS Game 4 to Saturday; Rays, Guardians to play Game 5 on Sunday
stories.summary: Game 4 of the ALCS was postponed late Friday night due to rain, creating an unusual set of circumstances for the Guardians and Rays.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- Game 4 of the American League Championship Series was postponed late Friday night due to rain, creating an unusual set of circumstances for the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays as the Milwaukee Brewers await in the World Series.

Friday's game was rescheduled for 8 p.m. ET Saturday. Game 5 was pushed to 5 p.m. ET Sunday, which was originally a scheduled off-day.

Game 4's pitching matchup will remain the same. All-Star hurler Nick Martinez will start for the Rays, and reliever Shawn Armstrong will open a bullpen game for the Guardians.

"It never cleared out the way they were hoping it would," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "It started to get later in the hour, and MLB and I think both clubs did everything they could to try to get it in. Made the most sense at this point and this hour, with no guarantee that there wasn't another band coming."

The Guardians hold a 2-1 series lead after winning 3-2 in Game 3 on Thursday. The first pitch for Game 3 was moved up from 6 p.m. to 1 p.m. ET to avoid inclement weather in the forecast.

The teams would play Game 6 on Monday and Game 7 on Tuesday at Tropicana Field, if necessary. If the series goes seven games, the clubs would play four games over four consecutive days in two cities.

The winner of the series will face the Brewers, who will have a week off after advancing to the World Series on Thursday. Game 1 of the World Series is scheduled for Oct. 23 in Milwaukee.

"This is what we do," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. "We play every day. Our guys get psyched or get cranked up an hour before game time. That never happened today. So it was a pretty calm day overall.

"These are professional baseball players. They know how to get ready. They know how to get going. I'm sure the Rays are in the same boat. Tomorrow is game day. Hopefully, there's no weather. I know it's going to be cold, but we'll be ready to play tomorrow night at 8:08."

stories.headline: 76ers, needing frontcourt help, convert 7-foot-6 Tacko Fall to two-way contract
stories.summary: The 76ers, dealing with injuries in the frontcourt, have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The 76ers have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract, the team announced Saturday.

Last month, the Sixers signed the 7-foot-6 center to an Exhibit 10 deal, and injuries to the frontcourt likely led to Fall getting this spot.

Ariel Hukporti, projected to be the Sixers' backup center, suffered a season-ending right Achilles tear in the preseason. Center Adem Bona, potentially the next man up, has been sidelined with a foot injury, and Dominick Barlow has battled back soreness that kept him out of the preseason.

Fall hasn't played in the NBA since the 2021-22 season, when he was with the Cleveland Cavaliers. This will be his fourth season in the NBA. He played his first two in Boston with new Sixers forward Jaylen Brown.

Fall, 30, most recently played for the Ningbo Rockets of the Chinese Basketball Association.

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Previews, storylines, betting info for all 14 games
stories.summary: Here's what you need to know ahead of Saturday's monstrous slate.
stories.body:
Tuesday was the 2026 edition of the NHL's Frozen Frenzy, with all 32 teams in action. On Saturday, 28 of 32 teams will be competing (including six at the magical start time of 7 p.m. ET), so maybe this is Frenzy Lite?

Regardless of the name, there are a number of fun storylines at play in Saturday's 14 matchups.

Here's a look at what you need to know for each contest, including betting info and broadcast details:

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

New Jersey Devils at Washington Capitals

1 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | WSH -125, O/U: 6.5

Two important points will be on the line here for a pair of clubs that missed the 2026 playoffs but have designs on getting back this spring. Will the high scoring keep rolling? The Devils netted seven on the Rangers on Thursday, while the Caps posted five on the Canadiens on Wednesday.

On the other hand, each team is dealing with injuries. The Caps will be without Pierre-Luc Dubois and Rasmus Sandin, and the Devils will be missing Luke Evangelista and Connor Brown.

Carolina Hurricanes at Winnipeg Jets

3:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CAR -170, O/U: 6.5

The defending champs have picked up right where they left off, racing out to a 6-1-1 record, just a point behind Vegas for tops in the league. The Jets have been one of the most pleasantly surprising teams this season, with a 4-1-2 record despite Connor Hellebuyck's continued absence. This will be Nikolaj Ehlers' second trip back to Winnipeg since signing with the Canes in summer 2025; he had an assist in a 4-3 win for the Canes last Nov. 21. What does he have in store for his old friends this time?

Vancouver Canucks at Tampa Bay Lightning

4 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | TB -380, O/U: 6.5

After an impressive opening pair of games against the Oilers, the Canucks have hit quite a skid. They've lost six straight and scored two or fewer goals in each contest. The Lightning have won five of their last six, averaging 3.33 goals in the stretch, and are undefeated at home this season. So in other words, that betting line above is not super surprising.

Seattle Kraken at Florida Panthers

6 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | FLA -185, O/U: 6.5

The Kraken took the Panthers' cross-state rivals to OT on Thursday but wound up with the loss. Can they finish the job on the Southern end of the state?

On the other side, Brady Tkachuk scored natural hat tricks in two straight games after going goalless in his first six games in a Panthers sweater. Can he repeat the feat again Saturday?

New York Islanders at Toronto Maple Leafs

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | TOR -142, O/U: 6.5

It's always a special occasion when two recent No. 1 picks face off, and that's exactly what hockey fans will get here. Matthew Schaefer, defending Calder Trophy winner and No. 1 pick in the 2025 draft, is in town to take on Gavin McKenna, Calder Trophy candidate and No. 1 pick in the 2026 draft.

Buffalo Sabres at Montreal Canadiens

7 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | MTL -142, O/U: 6.5

The Sabres and Canadiens had one of the most competitive series of the 2026 Stanley Cup playoffs, needing seven games to determine a winner. Then on Frozen Frenzy night, the teams needed a shootout to decide which would be the winner, with Zachary Bolduc netting the clinching tally for Montreal. Fans can hope that this contest in La Belle Province will be just as tightly contested.

San Jose Sharks at Detroit Red Wings

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DET -142, O/U: 6.5

Back when the Red Wings were in the Western Conference (yes, really), these two franchises met a fair amount in the playoffs: 1994, 1995, 2007, 2010 and 2011. A playoff matchup between the two these days would occur only in the Stanley Cup Final, so let's enjoy this one.

This is the final game in a string of seven out of eight at home for the Red Wings. The Sharks have four more games on their current road trip after this one.

Ottawa Senators at Philadelphia Flyers

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | OTT -142, O/U: 5.5

As well as the season has gone for Ottawa thus far -- a 6-2-0 record has them atop the Atlantic Division -- it has gone that poorly for Philly; the team that won a playoff series this past spring is still searching for its first win of the season in Game 10.

The goal suppression that was a key feature of the Flyers' run in the late season and playoffs has evaporated, and they enter Saturday giving up 3.56 goals per game. On the other side, the Sens' Linus Ullmark picked right up where he left off last postseason, with a perfect 6-0-0 record and stellar rate stats (1.20 GAA and .949 save percentage).

New York Rangers at Columbus Blue Jackets

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CBJ -135, O/U: 6.5

Despite the NHL's division-heavy playoff format, these two Metro rivals have never squared off in a postseason series. Maybe this is the year? Each has work to do. The Rangers need to stabilize their goaltending after Igor Shesterkin's injury and Dylan Garand's wobble against the Devils on Thursday, and the Blue Jackets need to get better at goal scoring and goal suppression. Will Columbus be able to solve Garand (or Spencer Martin) as often as the Devils did?

Dallas Stars at Chicago Blackhawks

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DAL -198, O/U: 6.5

Speaking of a surprising lack of playoff history, the Blackhawks and Stars have never squared off in the postseason since the North Stars moved to Dallas. Only the most optimistic residents of the 312 area code are thinking playoffs for the Blackhawks this season, so we anticipate that drought continuing.

But with Connor Bedard now back in the lineup, perhaps all things are possible. In his history, Bedard has five goals and two assists in eight games against the Stars. His new teammate Patrick Kane has scored 32 goals and 44 assists in 64 games against Dallas as a member of the Blackhawks.

St. Louis Blues at Nashville Predators

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | STL -110, O/U: 5.5

Both of these teams missed the playoffs by four points last season and should be in the mix again this April. The Blues score more goals than the Preds (3.57 per game vs. 2.57) but also give up a lot more (3.29 vs. 2.86). Who gets the upper hand after Saturday?

Boston Bruins at Los Angeles Kings

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | LA -142, O/U: 5.5

This will be the final leg of the Bruins' California road trip for 2026-27, after beating the Sharks on Tuesday and the Ducks on Friday. Like the Flyers, the Kings are still looking for their first win of the season, though they've played only five games thus far for some reason.

Perhaps Artemi Panarin can be a difference-maker for L.A. in this one. In 31 games against Boston in his career, he has 10 goals and 20 assists.

Edmonton Oilers at Utah Mammoth

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | UTA -148, O/U: 6.5

The Mammoth stampeded into Edmonton on Thursday and came away with a 4-2 win thanks to a pair of goals from captain Clayton Keller (one on the power play and the dagger into the empty net). The Oilers get a quick chance for vengeance here, with the setting shifting to the Delta Center in Salt Lake City.

Two seasons ago, Connor McDavid had seven points in three games against the Utah Hockey Club, and he followed that up with six points in three games in 2025-26 against the Mammoth. Does he have something big in store Saturday?

Pittsburgh Penguins at Vegas Golden Knights

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | VGK -230, O/U: 6.5

The NHL schedule makers wanted to get a tough stretch out of the way quickly for the Penguins this season; after a matchup against the Avalanche on Friday, they visit Vegas on Saturday and Utah on Monday, followed by a home date against the Panthers on Thursday. We may know a lot more about this club following that quartet of contests.

On the other side, the Knights have charged out to an early lead in the overall NHL standings with a 7-2-0 record on the strength of a plus-14 goal differential. Vegas has never had a player reach 100 points in a single season, but the player who has come closest, Jack Eichel, is on pace to do so. His 16 points through nine games are on pace for 149, which would shatter his franchise record of 94 set in 2024-25.

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Max Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant drive at Singapore GP

- Lewis Hamilton calls Singapore GP strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: Miami coach unbothered by Messi getting award in Spain 2 days before MLS game
stories.summary: Inter Miami coach Cristian "Kily" González confirmed Lionel Messi will travel to Spain next week to receive a prestigious award before rejoining the club for an MLS game two days later.
stories.body:
Inter Miami coach Cristian "Kily" González confirmed Lionel Messi will travel to Spain next week to receive the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, before rejoining the club for the match against the New York Red Bulls two days later.

Messi is due to attend the ceremony in Oviedo on Oct. 22 ahead of Miami's MLS game against the Red Bulls in Harrison, New Jersey.

- MLS Power Rankings: Miami back to winning ways, as Nashville chase history

- Garber won't dish on exchange with Messi: 'Between me and Leo'

But González said he had no concerns about Messi's travel schedule ahead of the game.

"Yes, he does have this event [in Oviedo], and I love that he will assume it in this way. The whole club agrees that he should be there because it is a terribly important award, not just for him but for his family," González told reporters on Friday.

"Then, of course, I will count on him for the game [against the New York Red Bulls]. Leo has the possibility, not an advantage, and I said it the other day after the match, I want him to be good.

"He needs this. He'll be there, then I will have him at the game so I'm not worried about that at all."

The Princess of Asturias Award recognizes individuals and institutions for notable achievements in fields like literature, social sciences, scientific and technical research, international cooperation and sports.

Messi became the first individual football player to be given the honor by the jury, which consists of several members -- including president of the foundation Teresa Perales -- when it was announced in June.

"The truth is that for me it is a great pride to be able to receive this recognition because of the importance it has and for the fact that it is recognized not only for what I do on the pitch but also off the pitch," Messi said when the award was announced.

"I am very happy, and very grateful. I wanted to let you know and send a big hug to everyone. Thank you and see you soon."

Inter Miami currently sits in second place on the Eastern Conference table and secured its place in the 2026 MLS playoffs on Wednesday.

Messi leads MLS' Golden Boot race with 23 goals, four goals ahead of nearest challenger Petar Musa of FC Dallas.

Ahead of the game at the Red Bulls, Miami will visit Atlanta United FC on Saturday.

stories.headline: Lisandro Martínez's Man United comments 'not that far off' but should not have been made - Peter Schmeichel
stories.summary: Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off."
stories.body:
Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off" but added he would not have liked hearing a teammate sound off in public.

Schmeichel was criticised for his handling of a post-match interview with Martínez in the aftermath of Tuesday night's 2-0 Champions League loss to Atlético Madrid, when the Argentina defender turned his fire on the club's hierarchy and named director of football Jason Wilcox as one of those from whom he "expects more."

Martínez spoke first to Amazon Prime's Gabriel Clarke before Schmeichel interviewed him for U.S. broadcaster CBS, with the defender repeating many of his criticisms while Schmeichel appeared to be trying to move Martínez on from the topic.

On Thursday Martínez issued a public apology for his comments and United said the matter was considered closed after the 28-year-old met with manager Michael Carrick, Wilcox and the club's hierarchy.

But inevitably the issue dominated Carrick's news conference on Friday with the substance of Martínez's comments still being debated.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Schmeichel said: "I would not like any teammate ever to go out and talk like that. Unless it was Bryan Robson... No, I wouldn't. I absolutely wouldn't like that.

"In the dressing rooms I was in, you were accountable. It just didn't happen very often that somebody stepped out of line, and of course we had a manager [Sir Alex Ferguson] who would not allow you to step out of line. He would react to that straight away...

"It's not that I completely disagree with what [Martínez] says. That's the other thing."

- Man United 'a circus' amid Lisandro Martínez rant - Roy Keane

Schmeichel then added: "Without going into too much detail about what Martínez said, some of the things he said are not far off.

"Look at the promising teams: Manchester City a long time ago, Arsenal for the past six years, Liverpool under Jürgen Klopp -- what did they do that suddenly changed the dynamics and changed their fortunes? They started at the back.

"They got in a goalkeeper, back four, a centre midfield player. They built that foundation, made it solid, and then they started to bring the creative players in. They've all done it... Built from the back. We've done the opposite, built from the front."

stories.headline: UFC champ Alexander Volkanovski proposes 'send-off' superbout vs. Justin Gaethje
stories.summary: UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski is calling for a "send-off" superfight against lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.
stories.body:
UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski has proposed a "send-off" superfight between himself and lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.

Volkanovski (28-4) is scheduled to defend his 145-pound title against Movsar Evloev (20-0) at UFC 333 on Oct. 24 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Arguably the greatest featherweight of all time, Volkanovski has acknowledged he is approaching the end of his career at 38 years old. Gaethje, 37, has acknowledged the same since he claimed the UFC's 155-pound title for the first time in June.

With both champions seemingly near the end of their time in the Octagon, Volkanovski has suggested a winner-take-all scenario in 2027.

"Imagine that, do it as a send-off," Volkanovski told the "Who Da Fook Are These Guys?" podcast. "Gaethje, Volk. I think he's said that he maybe has one more. That could be a superfight. Let's do a superfight with the lightweight title on the line. We can both see everyone off with a crazy superfight. That could be really good."

Volkanovski, of Australia, has already tried to capture the lightweight title. He famously challenged then-lightweight champion Islam Makhachev twice in a 10-month span in 2023. He suffered a razor-close decision loss to Makhachev in their first meeting in February then lost by first-round knockout in an October rematch that was scheduled on short notice.

Gaethje (28-5) has not even guaranteed whether he will fight again or retire off his historic win at the White House in June, but he has stated that he believes his next challenger would be lightweight contender Arman Tsarukyan. Volkanovski appears to be throwing his name into the mix in the hope of changing those plans.

"He's said, 'What's the point of doing rematches,'" Volkanovski said. "Let's do a superfight then [retire] straight away after, let the divisions sort themselves out. The UFC would be happy for that. Let's make it happen."

stories.headline: Tonga crush England in World Cup game of death
stories.summary: England's hopes of reaching the World Cup semi-finals are already on life support after suffering a 30-12 loss to world No.5 Tonga in their blockbuster showdown in Perth.
stories.body:
England's hopes of reaching the World Cup semi-finals are already on life support after suffering a 30-12 loss to world No.5 Tonga in their blockbuster showdown in Perth.

With His Majesty King Tupou VI and crown prince Tupouto'a 'Ulukalala among the sellout 18,302 crowd at HBF Park on Saturday night, Tonga produced a defensive masterclass in the four-tries-to-two victory.

The result put Tonga in the box seat to reach the semis, with games against Lebanon and Samoa to round out their group stage.

In contrast, world No.3 England have been left on the brink of elimination - even if they win their remaining two games against France and PNG.

Under the confusing group stage system employed for the World Cup, only two teams from across pools B and C will progress to the last four.

If England finish on the same amount of wins as Tonga, then the Pacific islanders will go through given they won Saturday's head-to-head battle.

Should England and Samoa end up with the same number of wins, the tiebreaker will be which nation has the better points-for-and-against differential.

Samoa opened their campaign with a 78-4 smashing of France, leaving England needing to post some massive wins in their remaining two games to stay alive.

It's why Saturday's clash between England and Tonga was dubbed the game of death - with the loser facing a mathematical tightrope to qualify past the pool stage.

There were plenty of big hits early, with England winger Zach Eckersley copping it big time after dropping a high ball and then being pummelled by a charging Dallin Watene-Zelezniak.

Stefano Utoikamanu opened the scoring in the 24th minute when he found a hole in England's defence to stroll over untouched.

A pair of Isaiya Katoa penalty goals extended the margin to 10 points by halftime, with England left to rue a series of fumbles and near misses.

England started the second half full of steam, resulting in a team-lifting try to AJ Brimson in the 46th minute.

But in a game where hard work was king, it was a slice of fortune that ended up giving Tonga a vital edge with Haumole Olakau'atu scoring the first of his two tries after he soccered the ball into an opponent's arm and then gathered the bouncing rebound.

And when Tuimoala Lolohea's neat dribble found Tolutau Koula in the corner to make it 22-6 in the 58th minute it was as good as game over.

The win was a powerful statement from Tonga, whose only previous taste of international success against England came in 2019 when they beat Great Britain.

stories.headline: Andoni Iraola questions VAR; says Szoboszlai, Frimpong out 'for some time'
stories.summary: Andoni Iraola questioned the decision to overturn a penalty awarded to Liverpool in the first half of their 2-1 win at Brentford and shared injury concerns over Dominic Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong after both were forced off.
stories.body:
LONDON -- Andoni Iraola questioned the decision to overturn a penalty awarded to Liverpool in the first half of their 2-1 win at Brentford and shared injury concerns over Dominic Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong after both were forced off.

Liverpool became the first team to defeat Brentford this season, with Keith Andrews' side finishing with nine men.

Brentford took the lead 44 minutes in through Keane Lewis-Potter, but the hosts finished the first half with 10 men after Yehor Yarmoliuk was sent off for a headbutt on Jérémy Jacquet.

Iraola's side made the numerical advantage count in the second half as Víctor Muñoz scored a wonderful equaliser with Bradley Barcola teeing up Alexander Isak for Liverpool's winner.

Brentford had a further player sent off when Vitaly Janelt was issued a second yellow card in the 92nd minute.

Overall Iraola was delighted with the win, but questioned a decision from the VAR to overturn a first half penalty. The referee awarded a penalty to Liverpool after Alexis Mac Allister was brought down by Dango Ouattara in the Brentford box, but the decision was overturned after Ouattara was seen to have made contact with the ball first.

"They're a very good team so to finish with three points here is really valuable," Iroala said. "The penalty situation -- I don't think it was a penalty. I don't think VAR should intervene as there was clear touch after.

"I remember Nottingham Forest earlier in the season -- it was a very similar situation where they said we are not going to intervene because there is contact. I think Dango arrived to touch the ball -- but the way they explained it after Forest is exactly that one and I don't think the VAR should intervene.

"We played very well against 10 men the minutes up until 2-1. We were patient, finding good positions. Probably more disappointed after we scored to make it 2-1 as then we felt like we have something to lose. [Until then] We were playing freely, we were finding good spots, we were sending a lot of players forward. But at 2-1, then we missed clear chances now to finish the game."

Iraola was delighted with the positions Barcola found himself in and was pleased with Florian Wirtz as well as Rio Ngumoha who made an impact off the bench.

"I think especially, I think the second half is the situation that if you need a player there you need Flo, no? It's like Rio is very similar: very few spaces, small pockets, time on the ball, something delicate things you have to find," Iraola said. "Players like Flo, Rio, Victor [Muñoz] was lovely -- they can make the difference."

But the win came at a cost. Szoboszlai was forced off in the first half, while Frimpong was introduced from the bench at half time, but lasted just five minutes before limping off injured.

"We have a very delicate situation," Iraola said. "We came from playing Champions League late at night and probably not a proper chance of recovery. You have doubt between players who have started two games and tired, or players recovering from injuries and not sure.

"Dominic felt the same injuries, not a new injury, so [it had] probably not healed enough. Jeremie injury is new. I thought playing against 10 he'd give us more heading forward. But it will mean we will lose Dom and Jeremie for some time."

For Andrews, he was pleased with how Brentford took the initiative when it was 11 versus 11, but admitted the red card changed things.

"There's a lot that went on in the game, obviously. We were edging it -- we were getting into a good rhythm -- starting to play with more belief and speed, thought and actions," Andrews said. "And we got ourselves in front. I felt confident -- the bench was strong and we were going to be able to make. But the sending off changes the dynamic of the game and we gave them an advantage."

- Alexander Isak completes Liverpool comeback at nine-man Brentford

- Florian Wirtz form can improve if Liverpool drop him - Steven Gerrard

- Transfer rumors, news: Are Liverpool the favorite to sign Bournemouth's Scott?

On Yarmoliuk's red card, Andrews said: "He's clearly disappointed. He's an amazing young man. We need to remember he is young and someone we love working with and want to try and develop. We need to look at ourselves first -- we don't tend to look at what part they play in the incident. I think they were cute and clever -- Yarmo needs to do better, and I can understand why that was a red.

"I've seen both of Vitaly's yellows back. I like our players playing with emotion and I like us to play on the edge and when you do that and you feel that some decisions aren't fair, that can be difficult for the players.

"Our players aren't robots. We have a spirit in our team that's really special. Could there have been a bit more consistency, perhaps."

On why he thought Liverpool were "cute and clever", Andrews answered: "If you look at where Jacquet is walking, he's not looking at the ball. He's walking into Yarmo. But we focus on us and our actions."

stories.headline: Dream's Angel Reese won't 'shy away' from big stage of WNBA Finals
stories.summary: Dream forward Angel Reese is embracing her first trip to the WNBA Finals with open arms, saying she's not about to "shy away from the moment" against the Valkyries.
stories.body:
OAKLAND, Calif. -- Angel Reese spent the better part of the past year manifesting a trip to the WNBA Finals. Now, she is just under 24 hours away from Game 1 of this year's championship series between her Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries.

In her first season with the Dream, Reese has had a career year.

Though veterans usually warn that the playoffs are a different beast, Reese has taken her production to another level in her first postseason stint.

"You have to be a playoff riser," Reese said at Finals media day Friday. "The greats are built for this. If you want to be considered the best player and well-respected, you can't shy away from the moment."

Reese is averaging 18.0 points, 8.4 rebounds, 2.2 blocks, 2.0 assists and 1.6 steals through five playoff games. The scoring and blocks have increased from the regular season, and she is shooting 38.5% from beyond the arc in the playoffs.

She has also been the anchor for the Dream's defense, which has been the best in the playoffs.

Although this is Reese's first time in the Finals, she is drawing on experience competing at high levels in college and with Team USA.

In September, Reese was a member of the gold medal World Cup team in Berlin. In 2023, she won an NCAA title with LSU.

"Anywhere I go, I am looking to win," Reese said. "I have won at every level I have been at. Coming into any situation, I have a winning mentality -- no matter what it looks like or what it takes."

stories.headline: Fantasy football Week 6 inactives: Hurts, Jackson ruled out; Flowers to play
stories.summary: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
stories.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists.

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 6 Buzz

Week 6 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 6

Biggest concerns ahead of Sunday

Players with early starts
Michael Penix Jr, QB, Falcons (ribs): Penix has been a full participant at practice all week long. He has been removed from the injury report and will start Sunday. Penix has yet to throw multiple TD passes or score 15 fantasy points in any game this season. He is purely for use in superflex formats, but his availability is great for Bijan Robinson and Drake London. Both are elite options with Penix under center.

Zay Flowers, WR, Ravens (toe): Flowers was added to the team's injury report Thursday but is not on the final report, meaning he will play in Week 6. His production took a hit without Jackson last week, but Flowers still saw nine targets in that game from QB Tyler Huntley, who will be under center again this week. Volume should keep him in play as a WR2. It's also worth noting that Rashod Bateman missed practice this week due to a shoulder injury but is also not on the final injury report, so he will play too. Rookie WR Ja'Kobi Lane is practicing in full and Jeremy Fowler reports he is "good to go" for Week 6. He is worth stashing if you have a bench spot available.

Caleb Williams, QB, Bears (hamstring): Williams has been a full participant at practice and is questionable in Week 6. He might opt to run less initially, but Williams is still in play as a QB1. I would use him over Trevor Lawrence, Jameis Winston and Jacoby Brissett. However, I would go with either Kirk Cousins or Jordan Love over Williams.

Quinshon Judkins, RB, Browns (ankle): Judkins missed practice to start the week before getting in a limited session Friday. He is questionable and his status truly seems to be up in the air for Week 6. If he sits, the Browns will be left with Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime on the active roster. McLaughlin is the preferred play and, while the floor is low, he'd be in the flex conversation due to volume. It's also worth noting that Dylan Sampson had his 21-day window for return opened this week, but he is out for Week 6.

KC Concepcion, WR, Browns (concussion): Concepcion has cleared the league's concussion protocol and will play in Week 6. Though we have seen flashes, Concepcion is more of an upside depth stash for now. Fantasy managers should instead go with some of the other streaming WR options listed in this article.

Denzel Boston, WR, Browns (foot): Boston was limited to start the week but no longer carries an injury designation, meaning he will play Sunday. The rookie is one of just 10 players since 2010 to have posted 330-plus yards and at least three touchdowns over their first five career games. He has seen at least seven targets in three of his last four games. That volume could turn to production against the Ravens, who have allowed the fifth-most WR yards. Boston is a strong WR2 play this week.

Tyler Warren, TE, Colts (groin): Warren popped up on the injury report Friday, which is never ideal. If he ends up suiting up, fantasy managers should play him as he has just one game with fewer than double-digit fantasy points, and he had nine in that game. However, it is not a bad idea to grab a streaming option now just to cover your bases. Some options are Tyler Higbee, Pat Freiermuth, Darren Waller and Michael Mayer.

A.J. Brown, WR, Patriots (ankle): The star receiver is questionable for Week 6. Ian Rapoport reports that the Patriots "will likely activate" Brown on Sunday. If Brown plays, he brings more risk than usual, but given all the byes and injuries, he'd be worth getting into starting lineups. While he brings upside and likely will see safe volume, it usually takes some time for a player to return to 100% after a high ankle sprain, so temper expectations a bit. If he sits, Romeo Doubs would be the top Patriots receiver and a boom-or-bust WR3 option.

Alvin Kamara, RB, Saints (back): Kamara might be questionable but he has been on the injury report all season long and not yet missed any time. However, he does not bring a ton of safety due to his lack of efficiency so far. That said, volume -- particularly in the passing game -- keeps him as a flex option.

Chris Olave, WR, Saints (illness): Olave missed practice to start the week due to an illness and is listed as questionable for Sunday. Still, it seems likely he will suit up. If he plays for the Saints, he plays for fantasy managers. If he sits, it means more volume for Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson. Both would be worth starting against the Giants.

Omar Cooper Jr, WR, Jets (ankle): The rookie is set to return from a Week 1 ankle injury that landed him on the IR. With Adonai Mitchell still sidelined, Cooper should operate as the Jets' No. 2 WR. Though he is not worth plugging into starting lineups just yet, he is worth a flier for those with an open bench spot in deeper leagues.

Kenyon Sadiq, TE, Jets (concussion): Sadiq is questionable for Week 6. He was able to log a full practice and HC Aaron Glenn said he expects him to play. Still, there are better streaming options this week such as Tyler Higbee, Juwan Johnson, and Pat Freiermuth.

DeVonta Smith, WR, Eagles (hamstring/toe): Smith was able to return to practice this week and is not on the final injury report, meaning he will play in Week 6. He will be more of a risk/reward play than usual given his team's downgrade at QB, but still in the WR3 range due to his big-play ability.

Dontayvion Wicks, WR, Eagles (hamstring): Wicks played through the injury Sunday and missed practice to start the week but is off the practice report. Given that Hurts is out for this one and Smith is back to be the WR1, fantasy managers should go in a different direction. Tre Tucker, Xavier Worthy, Germie Bernard and Khalil Shakir are better options.

DK Metcalf, WR, Steelers (illness): Metcalf has been removed from the injury report for Week 6. He is in play as a WR2.
Pat Freiermuth, TE, Steelers (calf): Friermuth was added to the injury report on Saturday and is questionable for Week 6. Still, a Saturday addition has him very much up in the air. If he were to miss, it would mean more volume for Metcalf and Bernard. Darnell Washington becomes a deep league streamer for those in need. At least he brings the chance at a touchdown.

Rico Dowdle, RB, Steelers (toe): This week, Dowdle was able to log his first full practice since injuring his toe. While he is questionable, that still puts him on track to play on Sunday. Still, Jaylen Warren has thrived in his absence, averaging 163 yards per game over the last three weeks. Mike McCarthy confirmed that Warren will remain the lead back. He should be started in all leagues. Dowdle should be rostered, but he's more of an insurance back until we see otherwise.

Tyjae Spears, RB, Titans (knee): After being limited Wednesday, Spears did not practice Thursday before logging a full session Friday. He is questionable heading into Week 6. He is coming off a season-high nine targets, although his usage has been too inconsistent to trust. His availability does impact Tony Pollard, who will see many of those passing downs if Spears is out. Pollard is a low-floor RB2, who will get a bump in upside if Spears sits.

Players with late starts
DJ Moore, WR, Bills (shoulder): Moore did not practice to start the week and returned Friday, once again wearing the red noncontact injury. He is questionable for Week 6. The Bills have their bye in Week 7 and could opt to let Moore take the extra time to recover. Last week in his absence, the Bills spread the ball around. Khalil Shakir is my preferred play of the other Bills receivers, as the Raiders rank top four for the most yards and touchdowns allowed to slot receivers. Keon Coleman is an upside flex option. The top Bills option to play would be Dalton Kincaid, as the Raiders have allowed the third-most TE touchdowns.

Ladd McConkey, WR, Chargers (foot): He is not on the practice report for Week 6, meaning he will play. How much he plays, however, is anybody's guess. He was active in Week 5 but did not play on a single snap. McConkey is a high-risk, somewhat high-reward type of play in Week 6. I'd prefer to stream players like Tucker, Worthy, Bernard or Shakir.

Quentin Johnston, WR, Chargers (chest): Johnston has practiced in a limited fashion this week and is not on the final injury report, meaning he will play in Week 6. Johnston has not surpassed 40 yards in any game this season. The Chargers' offensive line (and their offensive attack in general) is in shambles right now. It's best to use the streaming options listed above for McConkey.

Players on Sunday night
NONE

Players on Monday night
Stefon Diggs, WR, Commanders (hamstring): After missing Week 5, Diggs did not practice to start this week. However, he was able to return Friday. That gives him a chance to play Monday night. Terry McLaurin remains the top option in the Commanders' passing attack. It would probably be a good idea for managers risking a potential zero (by waiting on Diggs) to have a backup option in place. Brandin Cooks, Antonio Williams or Chig Okonkwo (who led the Commanders with six targets last week) are all options fantasy managers could nab off the waiver wire to cover their bases.

Terry McLaurin, WR, Commanders (hamstring): McLaurin was limited Thursday before logging a DNP on Friday. It is listed as rest, so fantasy managers should not panic just yet. However, with this game being Monday night, it would not be a bad idea to have one of the listed options above, just to cover your bases.

Mike Evans, WR, 49ers (ribs/Achilles): Evans is questionable heading into Monday night. He has been banged up a lot this season and continues to play through his injuries. He played through this same rib ailment last week. I would expect him to play, but fantasy managers should have a pivot option just in case. Brandin Cooks would be the top option on waivers, with Antonio Williams being another.

Ruled out before Sunday
Jeremiyah Love, RB, Cardinals (ankle): Love did not practice this week and is out for Week 6. Tyler Allgeier becomes an RB2 worth starting for volume alone. Allgeier would not only lead the Cardinals on the ground and see goal line usage, but he could see a good number of targets if they're in catch-up mode. I would play Allgeier over Woody Marks, Kamara, Omarion Hampton or Jacory Croskey-Merritt.

Lamar Jackson, QB, Ravens (ankle): Jackson did not practice this week and has been ruled out for Week 6. Tyler Huntley will once again start in his place. Last week, Huntley threw for 201 yards and two touchdowns, while running for 20 yards and a score. While he is more of an option for those in superflex leagues, it's nice to see that he brings upside.

For those in need of help in one-QB leagues, I prefer Jordan Love, Kirk Cousins, Tyler Shough, Jameis Winston and Jacoby Brissett. However, I would use Huntley over Daniel Jones, Geno Smith or as a Jalen Hurts replacement in two-QB formats.

Kyle Monangai, RB, Bears (thumb/toe): Monangai did not practice this week and is out for Week 6. The Falcons have been tough against the run, but his absence means more volume for D'Andre Swift. Despite the matchup, Swift is a must-play option at a beat-up RB position.

David Montgomery, RB, Texans (groin): Montgomery is out for the London matchup against the Jaguars. Woody Marks will start in his place. The Jaguars are an extremely tough matchup to run on, having allowed a league-low 42 RB rushing yards per game. They've allowed explosive runs at the second-lowest rate in football. The one thing going for Marks is that Jacksonville has allowed the fifth-most RB receiving yards. Some backs to play Marks over are Hampton, Kamara and J.K. Dobbins. Backs I would play instead of Marks are Braelon Allen, Emanuel Wilson, Pollard, Cam Skattebo and MarShawn Lloyd. The Texans have also ruled out WR Tank Dell for Week 6, but he is nearing a return.

Rashee Rice, WR, Chiefs (hamstring): Rice has not yet practiced coming out of the Chiefs bye and will not play in Week 6. With Rice out, expect Xavier Worthy to operate as the top receiver for the Chiefs, who are also without Tyquan Thornton. I would play Worthy over Ladd McConkey, Germie Bernard, Romeo Doubs and Jakobi Meyers. What this especially means is more targets for Travis Kelce, who is a must-start tight end. Cyrus Allen is worth a speculative add in deeper leagues.

TreVeyon Henderson, RB, Patriots (ankle): Henderson is currently expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks. That will mean more work for Rhamondre Stevenson, who had 16 touches, at least 74 yards and a touchdown in both of the last two games. He should be started for as long as Henderson is out. This is especially true this week against the Jets, who rank top eight in terms of the most rushing yards and RB fantasy points allowed.

Jalen Hurts, QB, Eagles (blood clot): This news caught the NFL world by surprise on Thursday and it's possible that Hurts will be out beyond just this week. However, Adam Schefter reports that the Eagles are not planning to put him on IR. Tanner McKee will be the Eagles starter, but he's only useful for desperate maangers in superflex leagues. Ideally, you can find better streaming options -- such as Cousins, Jordan Love, Shough, Winston or Aaron Rodgers. As for the Eagles' pass catchers, I'd look to go in other directions. Dallas Goedert would be the one to trust the most, just because the bar for TE success is so low. He's likely to be McKee's top target, especially in the red zone.

Will Shipley, RB, Eagles (foot): Last week's top waiver-wire pickup was injured after scoring a touchdown in London. He will be sidelined for multiple weeks. That leaves Dameon Pierce as the Eagles' lead back until Saquon Barkley returns. Pierce is a volume RB2/flex option in a fantastic matchup against the Panthers. Carolina ranks top four in terms of the most rushing yards, rushing touchdowns, yards after contact and RB fantasy PPG allowed.

Roman Wilson, WR, Steelers (finger): Wilson joins Michael Pittman Jr and Ben Skowronek as Pittsburgh players who have been ruled out for Week 6. That leaves Germie Bernard, who was a popular waiver-wire target this week, as the team's No. 2 receiver opposite of DK Metcalf. Bernard's style fits well with Rodgers and he can be used as a streaming option this week. Pat Freiermuth should also see a boost in volume and is a Week 6 TE streamer.

Deebo Samuel Sr, WR, 49ers (hamstring): The veteran receiver will not play in Week 6, but has thus far avoided the IR, which is a positive. The 49ers have a Week 8 bye, so it's possible we could see him return after that. It's worth mentioning that the 49ers have opened Christian Kirk's 21-day window to return, meaning he is closing in a comeback. As for Week 6, Brandin Cooks would be the go-to in-house replacement. However, previously listed outside streaming options are the way to go, if possible.

Ruled out before Monday
Jacory Croskey-Merritt, RB, Commanders (groin): JCM is out for Week 6. That leaves Rachaad White as the lead back for Washington. He is in the RB3 and flex range, but brings more upside due to the volume he will see, particularly in the passing game. It is a tough matchup as the 49ers have allowed explosive runs to backs at the lowest rate in the league and have allowed them to score just two rushing touchdowns this season.

stories.summary: First overall pick AJ Dybantsa exited the Wizards' preseason finale after injuring his ankle on an awkward landing and will undergo further evaluation.
stories.body:
First overall pick AJ Dybantsa exited the Washington Wizards' preseason finale Friday after injuring his ankle on an awkward landing and will undergo further evaluation.

Wizards coach Brian Keefe told sideline reporter Chase Hughes that Dybantsa had suffered a mild ankle sprain but that the decision to keep him out for the rest of the game was more precautionary.

"We'll look at it more when we get more information," Keefe said.

Dybantsa fell to the ground after landing on his left ankle following a midrange jump shot before limping to the locker room. He had scored 12 points in 15 minutes before his exit in the second quarter.

The Wizards open the regular season Wednesday against the Milwaukee Bucks.
